extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and practitioners) on handling rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 including disqualification of prior art under 35 U.S.C.103(c) (CREATE Act/joint research agreements), double patenting issues, form paragraphs to be used, and special rules for biotechnological processes under 35 U.S.C.103(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: CREATE Act / Joint Research Agreement (JRA) statement requirements (37 CFR 1.104(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke prior art disqualification under the CREATE Act, applicant must submit a statement that the prior art and the claimed invention were made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(3), that the JRA was in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made, and that the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should be on or begin on a separate sheet, must not be directed to other matters (37 CFR 1.4(c)), and must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). In addition to amending the specification to disclose the names of the JRA parties, the required statement must be submitted to properly invoke disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of disqualified prior art as commonly owned
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant disqualifies the subject matter relied upon by the examiner in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (as amended by the CREATE Act) and follows the rules, the examiner will treat the application under examination and the 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f), or (g) prior art as if commonly owned for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 103(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment affects double patenting analysis and which statutory grounds the examiner applies; see related guidance on double patenting and provisional rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for disqualification under 35 U.S.C. 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference used in an obviousness rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) that qualifies only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f), or (g) may be disqualified only when (A) proper evidence is filed, (B) the reference only qualifies as prior art under 102(e), (f), or (g) (i.e., not under 102(a) or (b)), and (C) the reference was used in an obviousness rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should verify these three conditions before treating a reference as disqualified under 103(c). If evidence of disqualification is provided, follow the examination procedure guidance in MPEP §706.02(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: JRA timing and scope requirements for disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: To disqualify a reference under the JRA provisions of 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the joint research agreement must be in effect on or before the date the later invention was made, and the claimed invention must have been made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) JRA in effect before invention and invention arises from JRA activities—disqualification possible; (2) JRA effective after invention date—cannot invoke JRA disqualification; (3) JRA limited to unrelated activities (e.g., covers invention Y but not X)—cannot invoke JRA disqualification. Ownership of inventions by separate parties does not, by itself, prevent invoking 103(c) if other requirements met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure when common ownership or JRA not established (examiner actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the file has not established that a reference is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner shall (A) assume the reference is not disqualified; (B) examine the application on all grounds other than any conflict arising from a possible 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) and/or (g); (C) consider applicability of references under 35 U.S.C. 103 including provisional rejections based on provisional prior art under 102(e); and (D) apply the best references against the claimed invention by rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 until the reference is disqualified under 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying references that qualify only under 102(e), anticipate that they may later be disqualified under 103(c). If a statement of common ownership or assignment is filed in reply to a 103 rejection and the claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made. See MPEP §706.02(l)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure when common ownership or JRA established (examiner actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application has established that the reference is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner will (A) examine the application as to all grounds except 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) and (g) (including provisional rejections based on provisional 102(e) art as they apply through 103); (B) examine for double patenting, including statutory and nonstatutory, and make a provisional rejection if appropriate; and (C) invite the applicant to file a terminal disclaimer to overcome provisional or actual nonstatutory double patenting if appropriate (see 37 CFR 1.321).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disqualification is established, do not treat the disqualified references under 102(e)/(f)/(g) as available prior art for 103(a) purposes; instead follow double-patenting and terminal disclaimer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting rejections and CREATE Act treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting rejections may arise between applications not owned by the same party as a result of the amendment of 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by the CREATE Act; for double patenting analysis, the application or patent and the subject matter disqualified under 103(c) will be treated as if commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection based on a pending application is provisional. Double patenting rejections can be overcome by disclaiming the terminal portion of the later patent’s term and, where appropriate, including a provision that the patent is enforceable only during common ownership (see 37 CFR 1.321). For non-commonly owned patents treated as commonly owned under the CREATE Act, a terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321(d) may obviate the rejection. See MPEP §§ 804 and 804.02 for more guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome applied art: derivation (37 CFR 1.132) or antedating (37 CFR 1.131)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may overcome applied art either by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed in the applied art was derived from the inventor of this application (and thus not an invention 'by another'), or by antedating the applied art under 37 CFR 1.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are standard rebuttals to applied prior art; examiners should consider such evidence when submitted and apply the appropriate rule to determine whether the reference remains available as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.20 — Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.20 quotes 35 U.S.C. 103(a) and forms the basis for all obviousness rejections set forth in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute need not be cited in all Office actions—only required in first actions on the merits employing 35 U.S.C. 103(a) and in final rejections. Use paragraph 7.20 only once in a given Office action, and it must precede form paragraphs 7.20.01–7.22 when used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections. Where the statute is applied but not cited, use paragraph 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.01 — 103(a) rejection using prior art under 102(e),(f), or (g) that is not disqualified under 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph must be included following form paragraph 7.20 in actions containing rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) using art that is disqualified under 103(c) using 102(e),(f),or (g) but which also qualifies under another section of 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify in the brackets the reference(s) sought to be disqualified. Use when the reference cannot be disqualified because it also qualifies under another subsection of 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.02 — Joint inventors; common ownership presumed
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application currently names joint inventors, the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time the inventions were made absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is advised of the obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates for claims not commonly owned so the examiner can consider applicability of 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and potential 102(e),(f) or (g) prior art under 103(a). This paragraph must be used in all applications with joint inventors (unless claims are clearly restricted to only one claimed invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.04 — Attempted disqualification via common ownership but missing statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this paragraph where applicant has attempted to disqualify a reference under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by showing common ownership but failed to provide a conspicuous statement that the application and the reference were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform applicant that required evidence must be filed to properly disqualify the reference under 103(c) and identify the commonly owned applied art in the brackets. Also note remedies under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.05 — Attempted disqualification via JRA but missing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this paragraph where applicant attempted to disqualify a reference under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by showing the invention was subject to a joint research agreement at the time made, but the applicant failed to provide required items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicant to file the missing requirements (e.g., required statement, specification amendments to name parties) in order to properly disqualify the reference under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Cite applicable rules 37 CFR 1.71(g) and 1.104(c) and MPEP §706.02(l). Identify in the brackets the reference sought to be disqualified and the reason(s) the disqualification is ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21 — Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over cited art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.20 or 7.103. An explanation applying the Graham v. Deere test must follow. If the rejection relies on prior art under 102(e), follow AIPA rules to determine the reference’s prior art date (with exceptions noted). If the rejection is a provisional 103(a) rejection based on a copending application, use paragraph 7.21.01 instead. If the applicability of the rejection prevents disqualification under 103(c), follow with 7.20.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21.01 — Provisional 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejection (common assignee or at least one common inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to provisionally reject claims not patentably distinct from a copending application having an earlier U.S. filing date and either a common assignee or at least one common inventor; the copending application would constitute prior art under 102(e) if published or patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection may be overcome by (1) a 37 CFR 1.132 showing of derivation, (2) a 37 CFR 1.131 showing of a date of invention prior to the copending application’s effective U.S. filing date, or (3) showing that the copending application is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Do not use 7.21.01 where the copending application is disqualified under 103(c) as of Dec 10, 2004. Use AIPA rules to determine 102(e) dates where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21.02 — 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejection, common assignee or at least one common inventor (how to overcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reference has a common assignee or at least one common inventor and constitutes 102(e) prior art, the 103(a) rejection might be overcome by: (1) a 37 CFR 1.132 derivation showing, (2) a 37 CFR 1.131 date of invention showing prior to the reference’s effective filing date, or (3) an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 stating current common ownership and prior inventor status together with a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note that showing the reference is disqualified under 103(c) will obviate the rejection. Insert --assignee-- or --inventor-- in the bracket as appropriate and provide an explanation of obviousness in the bracketed section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.22 — 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejection, further in view of
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to reject a claim under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over a primary reference as applied to another claim and further in view of an additional reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.21. An explanation applying the Graham v. Deere test must follow. If relying on 102(e) prior art, use AIPA rules to determine the prior art date where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graham v. Deere test for obviousness (¶ 7.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual inquiries for determining obviousness: (1) determine the scope and contents of the prior art; (2) ascertain differences between the prior art and the claims at issue; (3) resolve the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art; and (4) consider objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explanation applying these factors (Graham v. John Deere) must follow applicable 103(a) form paragraphs and may be used in response to arguments invoking Graham.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use a combined 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103(a) rejection (¶ 7.27) and illustrative circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 7.27 may be used to reject a claim under 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation) or alternatively under 103(a) as obvious. It is not intended for common use as a substitute for making the appropriate single rejection; a single rejection under 102 or 103(a) should be made whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances where 7.27 may be used include: (a) disputed claim interpretation where one interpretation yields 102 and another 103, (b) reference discloses all limitations except a property/function and examiner cannot determine inherent possession, (c) genus teaches a small genus placing the claimed species in the public, (d) product-by-process where product appears same despite different process, (e) means-plus-function uncertainty whether referenced element is equivalent or obvious variant, and (f) overlapping ranges where reference lacks a specific example in claimed range. A full explanation must follow the paragraph; if claim interpretation renders claims indefinite, consider a 112 rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim limitation relating to a tax strategy deemed within the prior art (¶ 7.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation interpreted as a strategy for reducing, avoiding, or deferring tax liability ('tax strategy') is deemed to be within the prior art pursuant to Section 14 of the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a limitation is so interpreted, recite the limitation in bracket 1 and the affected claim numbers in bracket 2; see USPTO memorandum 'Tax Strategies Are Deemed To Be Within the Prior Art' (Sept. 20, 2011) for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103(b) — applicability and requirements for biotechnological processes
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 103(b) provides that, upon timely election by applicant, a biotechnological process using or resulting in a composition of matter that is novel under 102 and nonobvious under 103(a) shall be considered nonobvious if (1) claims to the process and the composition are in the same application or in separate applications having the same effective filing date, and (2) the composition and process at the time invented were owned by or subject to assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional statutory requirements: (A) process and composition in same app or same effective filing date; (B) owned/assignable to same person when process was invented; (C) a patent on the process must also contain the composition claims or, if in separate patents, the patents must expire on the same date; (D) process must fall within the statutory definition of 'biotechnological process'; and (E) a timely election must be made by petition under 37 CFR 1.182. An election is normally timely if made no later than the earlier of payment of issue fee or filing of an appeal brief in an application containing an unaffected composition claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'biotechnological process' for 35 U.S.C. 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of 103(b), 'biotechnological process' means: (A) a process of genetically altering or otherwise inducing a single- or multi-celled organism to (i) express an exogenous nucleotide sequence, (ii) inhibit, eliminate, augment, or alter expression of an endogenous nucleotide sequence, or (iii) express a specific physiological characteristic not naturally associated with said organism; (B) cell fusion procedures yielding a cell line that expresses a specific protein (e.g., monoclonal antibody); and (C) a method of using a product produced by a process defined by (A) or (B), or a combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 103(b) applies only to biotechnological processes as defined. A petition under 37 CFR 1.182 must establish that all statutory requirements are satisfied. Election timing exceptions exist for certain patents/applications pending during the 1995–1996 timeframe; patentees may file reissue to correct errors in election when granted without deceptive intent. See MPEP §706.02(n) and case law (In re Ochiai, In re Brouwer) for further interpretation.
